I moved to Ecuador nearly seven years ago and I love my life here. Ask me anything.
I AM AN American Expat living in Ecuador. Ask me anything... en serio! Cualquier cosa :)

Did you know Spanish before you moved?

Where you familiar with the culture before you relocated?

That's a good question. I thought I knew Spanish before I arrived, but I soon found that that was another in a series of lies I had told myself. I only became proficient, like truly fluent, after about three years of living here. Part of that was because I didn't need to speak Spanish at all in the company that I worked for. When I moved to the high school, however, it was necessary to step up my game since I have to talk to parents and have meetings all in Spanish.

The culture was a big shock. On a visit, you kind of see the best of the culture because you're looking through rose-colored glasses. Living here will change your perspective quite a bit. I'm reminded of something I read about Kanye West saying that he was going to leave the US because of racism. I remembered thinking "Where will he go?? It's way more racist everywhere I've been down here". As a white guy, you experience racism also in a variety of forms here. It's not bad of course. Being a white male truly is like winning the cosmic lottery. I don't deny that. But being treated differently because of your skin color is a very weird feeling that I sympathize with a lot of people from the US for that have experienced that stuff on an institutional level for a long time.

TL;DR: Culture is definitely different and no I wasn't prepared for it!
Why Ecuador and are you happy with your decision?

I had visited Chile to see my ex girlfriend a year before coming here and it was my first time in S. America. I absolutely loved the way of life; the simplicity and the focus on family. Ecuador kind of found me. I was applying for jobs all over Latin America and an English institute hired me based here in Quito. It's a multinational company but if you're a native English speaker, there's no reason for you to have heard of it. After working there for a year, I was recruited into education at a high school that was looking for a Business and Management teacher for the IB program to give classes in English. The rest, as they say, is history. I'm super happy with my decision. There are some things I miss about US, but not much. (I had a baconator last time I went to visit my mom. WOW!)
Why, in your opinion, are latin american countries almost universally poor?

In my opinion, culturally Latin America is kind of slack. There's a lot of corruption because it's expected and somewhat tolerated. There's no respect for the law because from a young age you're not expected to follow the rules exactly. It's a bit of culture shock to get used to as an American living here, because we have a tendency to respect rules and authority.
